sources.attribution: Erickson GM, Gignac PM, Steppan SJ, Lappin AK, Vliet KA, Brueggen JD, Inouye BD, Kledzik D, Webb GJW (2012). Insights into the Ecology and Evolutionary Success of Crocodilians Revealed through Bite-Force and Tooth-Pressure Experimentation. PLoS ONE 7(3):e31781. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0031781. Claims are paraphrased; no figures or tables reproduced.

claims.text: The study measured 83 sexually mature individuals from 23 living crocodilian species recognized at publication; taxon-representative molariform bite-force values ranged from 900 N in Paleosuchus palpebrosus to 8,983 N in Crocodylus porosus.
claims.scope: Historical study sample and Table 1 taxon representatives; not the full modern COL26.8 accepted-species set.

claims.text: Body mass was the primary determinant of bite-force generation (phylogenetically corrected R²=0.87); rostral proportions accounted for only a small part of the remaining size-standardized variance, and Gavialis gangeticus was the low-relative-force outlier.
claims.scope: Cross-species comparative inference within the study's 2012 taxonomic sample.

gaps: The experiment does not determine diet, field bite performance, population-level distributions or current conservation status for every species.
The 2012 study's 23 species do not equal the 27 accepted living Crocodylia species in COL26.8; measurements under older taxon concepts are not reassigned to later-separated lineages.
